parts.answer: The maximum displacement of a particle or point on a wave from its equilibrium position.
accepted_alternatives: Maximum displacement from the rest position.

marking_points.text: Defines amplitude as the maximum displacement of a particle or point on a wave from equilibrium.

parts.answer: The minimum distance between two adjacent points on a wave that are in phase.
accepted_alternatives: The distance travelled by a wavefront or wave energy in one period.

marking_points.text: Defines wavelength as the minimum distance between adjacent in-phase points, or gives an accepted equivalent.

questions.answer: Energy travels with the disturbance while rope sections move locally.

option_feedback.A: This confuses motion of the disturbance with net transport of the rope.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The progressive disturbance transfers energy while each rope section oscillates locally.
option_feedback.C: Movement of the bead shows that energy, not rope matter, reached it.
option_feedback.D: The bead's motion is evidence that a disturbance and energy reached it.

marking_points.text: Selects B, identifying energy transfer with local motion of rope sections.

option_feedback.A: Amplitude is a positive maximum size, not the negative extreme displacement.
option_feedback.B: Zero is the equilibrium displacement, not the maximum displacement.
option_feedback.C: Correct. The greatest displacement from equilibrium is 4.0 mm.
option_feedback.D: 8.0 mm is the peak-to-peak distance, not the amplitude.

marking_points.text: Selects C, giving an amplitude of 4.0 mm.

questions.answer: They are not in phase because their directions of motion differ.

option_feedback.A: Equal displacement is insufficient when the points are moving in opposite directions.
option_feedback.B: Correct. In-phase points share both displacement and direction of motion.
option_feedback.C: A wavelength separation would make the directions agree as well as the displacements.
option_feedback.D: Their instantaneous directions do not determine their maximum displacements.

marking_points.text: Selects B, recognising that opposite motion directions mean different stages of the cycle.

parts.answer: The separation is 4.0 cm - 2.0 cm = 2.0 cm. This is 2.0/8.0 = 1/4 of a wavelength, so the phase difference is (1/4) × 360° = 90°.
accepted_alternatives: π/2 rad with a valid conversion to 90°

parts.answer: The progressive disturbance passes through neighbouring regions of water and transfers energy onward. Each water particle, including the water near R, oscillates locally about equilibrium rather than travelling with the ripple to S.
accepted_alternatives: An equivalent explanation separating travelling energy from local oscillation of the water.

marking_points.text: States that the progressive disturbance transfers energy through neighbouring regions to S.
States that water particles near R oscillate locally and do not travel to S.
